audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel / Shemuel Bet chapter 1, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for the messenger's conflicting Saul-death account, Amalekite identity, crown and bracelet, mourning, summary execution, the Bow lament, Jonathan-David love language, women mourners, Gilboa curse, and weapon-fall refrain.

verses.restored: After death of Saul, David returned from striking Amalek and stayed two days in Ziklag.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;

verses.restored: On third day, look, a man came from camp, from with Saul, with garments torn and earth upon his head. When he came to David, he fell to ground and bowed.

familiar.text: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.

verses.restored: David said to him, From where have you come? He said to him, From camp of Israel I escaped.

familiar.text: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.

verses.restored: David said to him, What was matter? Please tell me. He said, People fled from battle, and also many of people fell and died; Saul and Jonathan his son also died.

familiar.text: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.

verses.restored: David said to young man who told him, How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son died?

familiar.text: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?

verses.restored: Young man who told him said, By chance I was on mount Gilboa, and look, Saul was leaning upon his spear, and look, chariots and horsemen pressed close to him.

familiar.text: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.

verses.restored: He turned behind him, saw me, and called to me. I said, Look, I am here.

familiar.text: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I.

verses.restored: He said to me, Who are you? I said to him, I am an Amalekite.

familiar.text: And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.

verses.restored: He said to me, Please stand over me and put me to death, because agony has seized me, though all my life is still in me.

familiar.text: He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me.

verses.restored: I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew he could not live after his fall. I took crown that was upon his head and bracelet that was upon his arm, and I brought them here to my lord.

familiar.text: So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.

verses.restored: David took hold of his garments and tore them, and so did all men who were with him.

familiar.text: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:

verses.restored: They mourned, wept, and fasted until evening for Saul, for Jonathan his son, for people of YHWH, and for house of Israel, because they had fallen by sword.

familiar.text: And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.

verses.restored: David said to young man who told him, From where are you? He said, I am son of a resident alien, an Amalekite.

familiar.text: And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.

verses.restored: David said to him, How were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy anointed of YHWH?

familiar.text: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?

verses.restored: David called one of young men and said, Approach; strike him. He struck him, and he died.

familiar.text: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.

familiar.text: And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the LORD’s anointed.

verses.restored: David lamented with this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son.

translation_notes: The messenger's claim that he killed Saul conflicts with 1 Samuel 31, where Saul falls on his own sword. The narrative may portray a true report, a mercy-killing claim, opportunistic fabrication, or a separate tradition; the tension must remain visible.
The messenger is both Amalekite and son of a resident alien. His ethnicity does not explain guilt and must not support inherited enmity, xenophobia, or modern Amalek labeling.
David orders immediate execution based on the man's own testimony. The text provides no trial, witnesses, or opportunity for defense; this is summary royal violence, not a due-process model.
Saul's alleged request to be killed occurs under catastrophic battlefield injury. It may not become instruction for assisted death, suicide, or killing a distressed person.
David's lament honors Saul without erasing Saul's violence against David, Michal, Jonathan, priests, and civilians. Grief does not require historical absolution.
Jonathan's love is described as wonderful and surpassing the love of women. Queer readings may not be erased, while no single modern identity label should be forced upon the ancient relationship.
The lament's contemptuous circumcision language and silencing of Philistine women belong to ancient wartime rhetoric and may not authorize genital shame, misogyny, or ethnic hatred.
The final refrain calls warriors and weapons fallen; it is lament, not war recruitment.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not glorify the messenger's execution, use 'anointed' language to create leader immunity, or prescribe suicide/assisted death from the conflicting report. Preserve Jonathan and David's covenantal intimacy without queer erasure. Let lament hold love, anger, ambiguity, and accountability together.
